list.name: property
list.label: Property
list.query:
SELECT p.display_name || COALESCE(' [' || u.symbol || ']', '') || ' · ' || substring(p.topic from '([^/]+/[^/]+)$') AS __text,
       p.property_id AS __value
FROM config.vw_property_path p
LEFT JOIN config.machine_property mp ON mp.id = p.property_id
LEFT JOIN config.engineering_unit u ON u.id = mp.engineering_unit_id
WHERE NOT p.is_retired
ORDER BY p.topic

options.content: **Everything on this dashboard comes from the model.** Properties, names, units and alarm limits are read from the database, so a property added in Mathesar appears here without editing the dashboard. Times are shown in Melbourne time; they are stored in UTC (ADR-0003). Orange points mark values that are *uncertain* or *bad*; red dashed lines are the alarm limits from the model.

panels.title: Latest values
panels.description: Newest historian row of every property. Quality 'stale': nothing stored for more than twice the property's max publish interval (ADR-0007) - the source or the runtime is not delivering.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT p.display_name AS "Property",
       substring(p.topic from '([^/]+/[^/]+)$') AS "Machine / property",
       m.value AS "Value",
       u.symbol AS "Unit",
       CASE WHEN extract(epoch FROM now() - m.ts) * 1000 > 2 * mp.max_publish_interval_ms THEN 'stale'
            ELSE (ARRAY['good', 'uncertain', 'bad'])[m.quality + 1] END AS "Quality",
       m.ts AS "Time",
       extract(epoch FROM now() - m.ts)::int AS "Age (s)",
       (ARRAY['device', 'gateway'])[m.ts_source + 1] AS "Time source"
FROM config.vw_property_path p
LEFT JOIN config.machine_property mp ON mp.id = p.property_id
LEFT JOIN config.engineering_unit u ON u.id = mp.engineering_unit_id
JOIN LATERAL (SELECT * FROM hist.measurement h
              WHERE h.property_id = p.property_id
              ORDER BY h.ts DESC LIMIT 1) m ON true
WHERE NOT p.is_retired
ORDER BY p.topic

panels.title: $property

targets.rawSql:
-- One chart per property. Short ranges (under a minute per point) read raw
-- rows; longer ranges read the 1-minute or 1-hour averages (step 2.5), so a
-- month or a year loads quickly. From a minute per point, a point with no data
-- stays empty, so the line breaks where nothing was recorded (e.g. the stack
-- was off) instead of drawing across the gap; while OFM runs, the heartbeat
-- stores every value at least once a minute (ADR-0007). 'min'/'max' are the
-- extremes inside each point, drawn as a band; 'not good' marks uncertain or
-- bad values (ADR-0003); the alarm lines come from the model.
WITH src AS (
  SELECT ts, value, value AS vmin, value AS vmax, quality
  FROM hist.measurement
  WHERE property_id = $property AND $__timeFilter(ts) AND $__interval_ms < 60000
  UNION ALL
  SELECT bucket, avg_value, min_value, max_value, worst_quality
  FROM hist.measurement_1m
  WHERE property_id = $property AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND $__interval_ms >= 60000 AND $__interval_ms < 3600000
  UNION ALL
  SELECT bucket, avg_value, min_value, max_value, worst_quality
  FROM hist.measurement_1h
  WHERE property_id = $property AND $__timeFilter(bucket) AND $__interval_ms >= 3600000
),
points AS (
  SELECT time_bucket(make_interval(secs => $__interval_ms / 1000.0), ts) AS "time",
         avg(value) AS value, min(vmin) AS vmin, max(vmax) AS vmax, max(quality) AS quality
  FROM src
  WHERE $__interval_ms < 60000
  GROUP BY 1
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT time_bucket_gapfill(make_interval(secs => $__interval_ms / 1000.0), ts, $__timeFrom()::timestamptz, $__timeTo()::timestamptz) AS "time",
           avg(value) AS value, min(vmin) AS vmin, max(vmax) AS vmax, max(quality) AS quality
    FROM src
    GROUP BY 1
  ) gapfilled
  WHERE $__interval_ms >= 60000
)
SELECT points."time",
       points.value AS "value",
       points.vmin AS "min",
       points.vmax AS "max",
       CASE WHEN points.quality > 0 THEN points.value END AS "not good",
       p.alarm_low AS "alarm low",
       p.alarm_high AS "alarm high"
FROM points
CROSS JOIN config.machine_property p
WHERE p.id = $property
ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Short ranges show raw values. From one minute per point, 1-minute or 1-hour averages, with a grey band from the lowest to the highest value inside each point; the line breaks where nothing was recorded. Orange: not good. Red dashed: alarm limits from the model.
